clue.text: Parents on the outskirts of an American country

indicators.note: something on the outskirts of another sits around its edges, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: pa is one parent, a father
taken as written
ma is the other parent, a mother

explanation.surface: Someone's mother and father live on the fringes of an American town.
explanation.walkthrough: One word, 'Parents', supplies two pieces here, one for each parent, and the first of them wraps around the plain word 'an'.
explanation.definitionFit: Panama is a nation in Central America, so it is an American country.

clue.text: Gather team as serving drinks

indicators.note: something that drinks takes liquid in, so these words take the solution inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the three words, from inside 'team' to the start of 'serving'

explanation.surface: A team is gathered together while handing round drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to collect or accumulate, a direct synonym of gather.

clue.text: Learn art in case appearing crafty

indicators.note: something crafty is cunningly contrived, so the letters are worked into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A student picks up art skills in a situation that seems sly or cunning.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascertain is to find out for certain, which is one sense of learn.

clue.text: A part of song, hostile

parts.note: taken as written
a verse is a section of a song

explanation.surface: A section of a song turns out to be hostile in tone.
explanation.definitionFit: Being averse to something means being opposed to it, close in sense to hostile.

clue.text: Completely destroyed, Dynamic Duo and I wept

indicators.note: dynamic means full of energy and movement, so the letters are set in motion into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
joins the two parts of the fodder

explanation.surface: Batman and Robin, the Dynamic Duo, were utterly defeated and the speaker wept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dynamic Duo' reads as a fixed phrase for Batman and Robin, but 'Dynamic' is only the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To be wiped out is to be annihilated, so it fits completely destroyed.

clue.text: Somewhere in Somerset, old actress riding thoroughbred?

parts.note: Mae West, Hollywood star of the 1930s
riding a horse is being on it
a fine female horse might whimsically be called a super mare; the question mark flags the play

explanation.surface: A veteran film star is out riding a fine racehorse in the West Country.
explanation.walkthrough: Weston-super-Mare is a seaside town in Somerset, a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The town lies on the Somerset coast, so it is one example of a place in that county.

clue.text: Country history test

parts.note: one's history is one's past
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: An exam on a nation's history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' looks like a noun, a nation, but it is the adjective, meaning rural.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastoral describes rural life and landscape, so it matches country used as an adjective.

clue.text: Tube blocked by a coin, once

indicators.note: a pipe blocked by something has that thing lodged within it

parts.note: a duct is a tube or channel
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pipe gets clogged when someone drops a coin down it.
explanation.definitionFit: The ducat was a gold or silver coin used across Europe in past centuries.

clue.text: In the raw -— like a plain salad?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: naked, wearing no clothes
second meaning: served with no dressing poured over it

explanation.walkthrough: 'In the raw' suits food too, which is what makes the two halves seem one idea about salad.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means unclothed, and also describes a salad served without any dressing.

clue.text: Criticise wrinkles in body parts

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly
creases are wrinkles or folds

explanation.surface: Someone complains about wrinkles on parts of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: The pancreas is a gland, an organ of the body; the plural names more than one such organ.

clue.text: Fish with a tail end

parts.note: a cod is a fish
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fish with a tail at its back end.
explanation.definitionFit: A coda is the closing passage of a piece of music, so it is the concluding section.

clue.text: Teas oddly dismissed, posers ordered coffee

indicators.note: dismissing the odd-numbered letters leaves only those in even positions

parts.note: the second and fourth letters remain

indicators.note: ordered means put into an arrangement, so these letters are set in a new sequence

parts.note: the six letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A café throws out the tea, and some show-offs order coffee instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Espresso is strong black coffee made by forcing steam through ground beans.

clue.text: Exposed place for birth

parts.note: something out in the open is exposed
to set something is to place it

explanation.surface: A spot left open to the elements where a baby is delivered.
explanation.definitionFit: Birth is the beginning of something, and the outset is its start.

clue.text: Reportedly, take off tiny jumper

indicators.note: reportedly means as told by others, pointing to how a word sounds when spoken

parts.note: to take off is to run away, to flee

explanation.surface: Supposedly, you should remove a little sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumper is the British word for a sweater, which is the misleading reading here; the tiny jumper is an insect that leaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A flea is a small insect famous for jumping huge distances relative to its size.

clue.text: Immediately, love equally exciting

parts.note: to love something is, mildly, to like it
as in 'as good', meaning equally good
hot can mean thrilling or exciting

explanation.surface: Someone instantly finds love and excitement in equal measure.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something like a shot is an idiom for doing it at once, without hesitating.

clue.text: Make-up has run, being sloppy

parts.note: slap is British slang for cosmetics
to dash is to run

explanation.surface: Someone's mascara has run, so they look a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' reads as smudged make-up, but it means to sprint; slap is informal British for make-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapdash means careless and hurried, so it is a synonym for sloppy.

clue.text: With the current club, confess manacled

indicators.note: manacled means chained up, so one word is held captive inside the other

parts.note: a driver is a golf club
to own up is to confess, so own alone can mean admit

explanation.surface: A modern club whose members admit to being chained up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With the current' looks like 'up to date', but here it means the flow of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Going downriver means travelling in the direction the water flows, with the current.

clue.text: Fresh lemon is put on a pudding

indicators.note: fresh means new, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: the seven letters to rearrange
taken as written, placed at the end below the rest

explanation.surface: A fresh lemon is set on top of a dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Semolina is a milk pudding made with coarse wheat grains, a classic British school dessert.

clue.text: Superficial type in soak

indicators.note: in places one word inside another

parts.note: to seep is to soak through
a type is a kind

explanation.surface: A shallow sort of person sits in a bath.
explanation.definitionFit: Something skin-deep goes no further than the surface, so it is superficial.

clue.text: With difficulty, progress measured, we hear?

indicators.note: we hear means what follows is judged by its sound when spoken

parts.note: to measure a load on scales is to weigh it

explanation.surface: Someone's progress, carefully measured, was hard going.
explanation.definitionFit: To wade is to walk slowly through water or mud, or to make laborious progress.

clue.text: Originally, birch or yew proving flexible for old weapons manufacturer

indicators.note: originally points to the very first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: its first letter

indicators.note: something flexible can be bent into new shapes, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: the five letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A weapon-maker of old tests whether birch or yew bends best.
explanation.walkthrough: Yew was the wood of the English longbow, so the surface sits squarely in the craftsman's workshop.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowyer was a craftsman who made bows, the archer's weapon.

clue.text: Bun, say: tricky eating one with starter of offal

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so one word goes into the other

parts.note: a tricky task is hard
the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the starter is the first course, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: its first letter

explanation.surface: A meal of a bread roll, tricky to eat with some liver to begin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bun' and 'offal' set up a food scene, but a bun is a hairstyle.
explanation.definitionFit: A bun is a style of hair gathered into a knot, so it is one example of a hairdo.

clue.text: Tree in central part of Europe, white

indicators.note: central part means only the letters at the middle of the word are kept

parts.note: its two middle letters
a wan face is pale or white

explanation.surface: A pale-barked tree growing in the heart of Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: The rowan, or mountain ash, is a tree with red berries.

clue.text: Frame in car OK for going abroad

indicators.note: going abroad is travelling widely, so the letters wander out of their order

parts.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A picture frame in a car is fine to take on a trip overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: A roof rack is a metal framework fixed on top of a car to carry luggage.

clue.text: Vessel on a lake, artificial waterway

parts.note: a can is a container, a vessel
taken as written
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A boat floats on a lake by a man-made channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a boat, but here it is a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A canal is a channel dug for boats or irrigation, a waterway built by people.

clue.text: Dog food

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a Chinese breed with a blue-black tongue
second meaning: informal word for grub

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it is just pet food; separately it is a breed and a slang word for something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names the chow chow breed and is also casual slang for a meal.

clue.text: Where athletes randomly entered, no matter what?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: competitors put into a race chosen at random

explanation.walkthrough: The first half reads the phrase literally, as an event at a sports meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning whatever happens, regardless of circumstances.

clue.text: Primitive mood in philosopher

indicators.note: in places one word inside another

parts.note: a sage is a wise thinker
the tone of something is its mood

explanation.surface: A thinker falls into a basic, gloomy frame of mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Stone-age describes the earliest era of human tools, so figuratively it means crude or primitive.

clue.text: A bank seen on far side of river, very little

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river
taken as written
to bank on something is to rely on it

explanation.surface: A riverbank is glimpsed on the far side, though barely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On far side of river' places A and the word for bank after R.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarely means hardly ever, and very little works as an adverb of frequency in that sense.
